sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Administrative Centralization**: Shift from decentralized Mughal administration to a rigid, hierarchical **Bureaucratic Structure** designed for revenue collection and law enforcement.
• **Rule of Law**: Introduction of **Formal Legal Codes** (IPC, CrPC) which replaced personal/customary laws, primarily serving colonial interests rather than egalitarian justice.
• **Commercialization of Administration**: The administration was essentially a **'Police State'** where the primary objective was the protection of trade routes and tax extraction.
• **Key Metric**: The **Drain of Wealth** theory (Dadabhai Naoroji) serves as the primary analytical lens to evaluate the economic impact of these administrative policies.

The principle that law is supreme; in the Indian context, it meant the end of arbitrary power but also the introduction of a legal system that favored the wealthy and the British.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Police Reforms**: Creation of the Thana system (Cornwallis) to replace local Zamindari policing.
• **Infrastructure**: Development of Railways and Telegraphs (Dalhousie) primarily for military mobility and market penetration.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Alienation of the masses, destruction of traditional village self-sufficiency, and racial discrimination in the judiciary.
• **Solutions**: Post-1857, the British shifted to a policy of 'Association' (Indian Councils Act 1861) to mitigate administrative instability.

items.title: Mnemonic for Land Revenue
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-R-M' (Permanent, Ryotwari, Mahalwari).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P (Permanent - Bengal/Cornwallis), R (Ryotwari - Madras/Munro), M (Mahalwari - North/Holt Mackenzie).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Rule of Law' with 'Equality before Law'. The British legal system introduced the former but systematically violated the latter through racial discrimination (e.g., Ilbert Bill controversy).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Administrative Colonialism' to describe how the British used the bureaucracy as a tool for socio-economic engineering rather than public service.

keyTakeaways: British administration was designed for extraction, not development.
The legal and bureaucratic framework created a 'Steel Frame' that prioritized stability over social welfare.
Land revenue systems were the primary mechanism for the destruction of the traditional Indian agrarian economy.
